events.title: DEC PDP-8 unveiled
events.summary: Digital Equipment Corporation unveiled the PDP-8 on March 22, 1965 — the first commercially successful minicomputer, with shipments beginning in April 1965.
events.about: The PDP-8 was small enough and cheap enough ($18,000) for labs, factories, and universities to own their own computer. Teams programmed in assembly and BASIC on teletypes; DEC's minicomputer line trained a generation of systems programmers before PCs arrived. Unix and C were developed on PDP machines at Bell Labs.

narrative.whyChosen: The PDP-8 created the minicomputer category and democratized access beyond mainframe datacenters.
narrative.whyImportant: It put interactive computing in departments that could never afford IBM mainframes.
narrative.problemSolved: Organizations needed local computing power without million-dollar centralized machines.
